title: Achaemenid Persian Rule
description: The region of modern Afghanistan, including Bactria and Arachosia, became part of the Achaemenid Persian Empire under Darius I.

title: Alexander the Great Conquers Bactria
description: Alexander the Great campaigned through the region, founding cities and bringing Hellenistic influence to Bactria and Sogdiana.

title: Greco-Bactrian Kingdom
description: A Hellenistic state emerged in Bactria, blending Greek and local cultures and minting renowned coinage.

title: Founding of the Durrani Empire
description: Ahmad Shah Durrani united Pashtun tribes and founded the Durrani Empire, often seen as the origin of modern Afghanistan.

title: Independence from British Influence
description: Following the Third Anglo-Afghan War, Afghanistan regained full control of its foreign affairs under Amanullah Khan.

title: Soviet Invasion
description: The Soviet Union invaded Afghanistan, beginning a decade-long war that caused immense devastation and displacement.

title: Fall of the Taliban Regime
description: A US-led coalition removed the Taliban from power following the September 11 attacks, beginning a new political era.

title: Founding of Erebuni Fortress
description: King Argishti I of Urartu founded the fortress of Erebuni, considered the origin of Armenia's capital Yerevan.

title: Kingdom of Greater Armenia
description: Artaxias I founded the Artaxiad dynasty, establishing an independent Armenian kingdom that later expanded under Tigranes the Great.

title: First Nation to Adopt Christianity
description: Armenia became the first state to adopt Christianity as its official religion under King Tiridates III.

title: Creation of the Armenian Alphabet
description: Mesrop Mashtots created the Armenian alphabet, enabling a flourishing of national literature and identity.

title: Armenian Genocide
description: The Ottoman Empire carried out the systematic deportation and mass killing of around 1.5 million Armenians.

title: Independence from the Soviet Union
description: Armenia declared independence as the USSR dissolved, becoming a sovereign republic.

title: Spitak Earthquake
description: A devastating earthquake struck northern Armenia, killing tens of thousands and destroying entire towns.

title: Kingdom of Caucasian Albania
description: Caucasian Albania, an ancient state in the region of modern Azerbaijan, emerged and later adopted Christianity.

title: Rise of the Atabegs of Azerbaijan
description: The Eldiguzid (Atabeg) dynasty established a powerful state in the region, a flourishing period of Persian-influenced culture.

title: Poet Nizami Ganjavi
description: Nizami Ganjavi, one of the greatest Persian-language poets, lived and worked in Ganja, leaving a lasting literary legacy.

title: Treaty of Gulistan
description: The treaty between Russia and Persia transferred much of present-day Azerbaijan to the Russian Empire.

title: Azerbaijan Democratic Republic
description: Azerbaijan declared independence, becoming the first secular democratic republic in the Muslim world and granting women suffrage.

title: Independence from the Soviet Union
description: Azerbaijan restored its independence following the collapse of the Soviet Union.

title: Contract of the Century
description: Azerbaijan signed a major oil agreement with international companies, transforming its economy through Caspian petroleum.

title: Ancient Mauryan Bengal
description: The region of Bengal, including ancient Pundravardhana, became part of the Mauryan Empire and an early urban center.

title: Rise of the Pala Empire
description: The Buddhist Pala dynasty unified Bengal and became a major patron of learning, art, and Buddhism in South Asia.

title: Mughal Conquest of Bengal
description: The Mughal Empire annexed Bengal, which became one of its wealthiest and most productive provinces.

title: Battle of Plassey
description: The British East India Company defeated the Nawab of Bengal, beginning British colonial dominance over the region.

title: Partition and East Pakistan
description: The partition of British India created East Bengal as part of Pakistan, separated from West Pakistan by India.

title: Bengali Language Movement
description: Protests demanding recognition of Bengali led to deaths in Dhaka, later commemorated as International Mother Language Day.

title: Liberation War and Independence
description: Bangladesh won independence from Pakistan after a brutal nine-month war led by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.

title: Unification by Zhabdrung
description: Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal unified Bhutan and established a dual system of religious and civil governance.

title: Construction of Punakha Dzong
description: The Punakha Dzong was built as a fortress-monastery, becoming a center of Bhutanese government and Buddhist culture.

title: Founding of the Wangchuck Monarchy
description: Ugyen Wangchuck was crowned the first hereditary king of Bhutan, unifying the country under a single monarchy.

title: Bhutan Joins the United Nations
description: Bhutan became a member of the United Nations, expanding its presence on the international stage.

title: Gross National Happiness Concept
description: King Jigme Singye Wangchuck introduced Gross National Happiness as a guiding philosophy of national development.

title: Introduction of Television and Internet
description: Bhutan became one of the last nations to introduce television and the internet, opening to global media.

title: Transition to Democracy
description: Bhutan held its first national parliamentary elections, transitioning from absolute monarchy to constitutional democracy.

title: Rise of the Bruneian Sultanate
description: Brunei emerged as a powerful Islamic sultanate controlling trade across coastal Borneo and beyond.

title: Magellan Expedition Visits Brunei
description: Survivors of Magellan's expedition visited the wealthy court of Brunei, documenting its splendor and power.

title: British Protectorate Established
description: Brunei became a British protectorate, preserving the sultanate while ceding control of foreign affairs.

title: Discovery of Oil at Seria
description: Major oil reserves were discovered at Seria, transforming Brunei into one of the wealthiest states in the region.

title: First Written Constitution
description: Brunei adopted its first written constitution, granting internal self-government while remaining a British protectorate.

title: Full Independence
description: Brunei gained full independence from Britain, with Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah as head of state.

title: Introduction of Sharia Penal Code
description: Brunei began implementing a Sharia-based penal code, the first East Asian nation to do so at the national level.

title: Founding of the Khmer Empire
description: Jayavarman II declared himself universal monarch, founding the Khmer Empire that dominated Southeast Asia.

title: Construction of Angkor Wat
description: King Suryavarman II began building Angkor Wat, the largest religious monument in the world.

title: Fall of Angkor
description: The Siamese sacked Angkor, prompting the Khmer to abandon the capital and shift power southward.

title: French Protectorate
description: Cambodia became a French protectorate, beginning nearly a century of colonial rule under French Indochina.

title: Independence from France
description: Cambodia gained full independence from France under King Norodom Sihanouk.

title: Khmer Rouge Takeover
description: The Khmer Rouge seized power and carried out a genocide that killed an estimated 1.7 to 2 million people.

title: Restoration of the Monarchy
description: Following UN-administered elections, Cambodia restored its constitutional monarchy and adopted a new constitution.

title: Shang Dynasty
description: The Shang dynasty arose along the Yellow River, producing the earliest known Chinese writing and bronze casting.

title: Birth of Confucius
description: The philosopher Confucius was born, founding a tradition of ethics and governance that shaped East Asian civilization.

title: Unification under the Qin Dynasty
description: Qin Shi Huang unified China into the first centralized empire and standardized writing, currency, and measures.

title: Opening of the Silk Road
description: Under Emperor Wu of Han, trade routes connecting China to Central Asia and Europe flourished.

title: Invention of Paper
description: Cai Lun refined papermaking during the Han dynasty, revolutionizing the recording and spread of knowledge.

title: Voyages of Zheng He
description: Admiral Zheng He led massive maritime expeditions across the Indian Ocean, projecting Ming power and trade.

title: Fall of the Qing Dynasty
description: The Xinhai Revolution ended over two thousand years of imperial rule and established the Republic of China.

title: Founding of the People's Republic
description: Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China after the Communists won the civil war.

title: Mycenaean Greek Settlement
description: Mycenaean Greeks settled Cyprus, establishing the Greek cultural and linguistic roots of the island.

title: Assyrian Influence over Cypriot Kingdoms
description: The independent city-kingdoms of Cyprus paid tribute to Assyria, reflecting the island's strategic trade position.

title: Roman Annexation
description: Cyprus was annexed by the Roman Republic, becoming a prosperous province known for copper and trade.

title: Ottoman Conquest
description: The Ottoman Empire captured Cyprus from Venice, beginning three centuries of Ottoman rule.

title: British Administration Begins
description: Britain took over administration of Cyprus from the Ottomans, later formally annexing it.

title: Independence from Britain
description: Cyprus became an independent republic with a power-sharing constitution between Greek and Turkish Cypriots.

title: Division of the Island
description: A Greek-backed coup and subsequent Turkish invasion divided Cyprus, a partition that endures today.

title: Accession to the European Union
description: Cyprus joined the European Union, though EU law is suspended in the northern part of the divided island.

title: Kingdom of Kartli (Iberia)
description: The Kingdom of Iberia emerged in eastern Georgia, becoming an important Caucasian state.

title: Adoption of Christianity
description: King Mirian III made Christianity the state religion of Iberia after the mission of Saint Nino.

title: Reign of David the Builder
description: David IV reunified Georgia and ushered in a medieval golden age of culture and military strength.

title: Golden Age under Queen Tamar
description: Queen Tamar's reign marked the height of Georgian power, expansion, and cultural achievement.

title: Russian Annexation
description: The Russian Empire annexed the Georgian kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti, ending centuries of independence.

title: Democratic Republic of Georgia
description: Georgia declared independence and established a democratic republic, lasting until Soviet invasion in 1921.

title: Independence from the Soviet Union
description: Georgia restored its independence as the Soviet Union collapsed.

title: Rose Revolution
description: A peaceful revolution forced President Shevardnadze to resign, ushering in pro-Western democratic reforms.

title: Indus Valley Civilization
description: The Indus Valley Civilization flourished with planned cities like Harappa and Mohenjo-daro and advanced urban infrastructure.

title: Birth of the Buddha
description: Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, was born, founding Buddhism which spread across Asia and the world.

title: Founding of the Maurya Empire
description: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire, the first to unify most of the Indian subcontinent.

title: Gupta Empire Golden Age
description: The Gupta Empire ushered in a golden age of mathematics, astronomy, art, and the concept of zero.

title: Founding of the Mughal Empire
description: Babur won the Battle of Panipat and founded the Mughal Empire, which shaped Indian art and architecture.

title: British Crown Rule (the Raj)
description: After the 1857 rebellion, the British Crown assumed direct rule over India, beginning the British Raj.

title: Independence and Partition
description: India gained independence from Britain, accompanied by the partition that created Pakistan.

title: Adoption of the Constitution
description: India adopted its constitution and became a sovereign democratic republic, the world's largest democracy.

title: Rise of Srivijaya
description: The maritime empire of Srivijaya emerged on Sumatra, dominating trade and Buddhist learning across the region.

title: Construction of Borobudur
description: The vast Buddhist temple of Borobudur was built in central Java, a masterpiece of ancient architecture.

title: Founding of the Majapahit Empire
description: The Majapahit Empire rose in Java, becoming the largest Hindu-Buddhist empire in Southeast Asian history.

title: Dutch East India Company Arrives
description: The Dutch East India Company established trading dominance, beginning centuries of colonial control.

title: Eruption of Krakatoa
description: The catastrophic eruption of Krakatoa killed tens of thousands and affected global climate.

title: Declaration of Independence
description: Sukarno and Hatta proclaimed Indonesian independence from Dutch colonial rule.

title: Indian Ocean Tsunami
description: A massive earthquake and tsunami devastated Aceh and other coastal regions, killing over 160,000 in Indonesia.

title: Legendary Founding by Emperor Jimmu
description: Tradition holds that Emperor Jimmu founded the Japanese imperial line, the basis of the world's oldest monarchy.

title: Introduction of Buddhism
description: Buddhism was introduced from Korea, profoundly shaping Japanese religion, art, and culture.

title: Establishment of the Kamakura Shogunate
description: Minamoto no Yoritomo founded the first shogunate, beginning centuries of rule by the samurai military class.

title: Tokugawa Shogunate Begins
description: Tokugawa Ieyasu established the Edo shogunate, ushering in over two centuries of peace and isolation.

title: Meiji Restoration
description: Imperial power was restored and Japan launched rapid modernization and industrialization.

title: Atomic Bombings and Surrender
description: The atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki led to Japan's surrender, ending World War II.

title: Tokyo Olympic Games
description: Japan hosted the Summer Olympics and unveiled the Shinkansen bullet train, symbolizing its postwar revival.

title: Scythian and Saka Nomads
description: The Saka and other nomadic peoples flourished on the Kazakh steppe, leaving rich burial mounds and goldwork.

title: Mongol Conquest
description: Genghis Khan's armies conquered the region, which later became part of the Mongol Empire and the Golden Horde.

title: Founding of the Kazakh Khanate
description: The Kazakh Khanate was established, uniting Kazakh tribes and forming the basis of Kazakh national identity.

title: Russian Protection of the Junior Zhuz
description: Kazakh tribes began accepting Russian protection, leading gradually to absorption into the Russian Empire.

title: Baikonur Cosmodrome Established
description: The Soviet Union built Baikonur in Kazakhstan, later the launch site of the first human spaceflight.

title: Independence from the Soviet Union
description: Kazakhstan declared independence, becoming the last Soviet republic to do so as the USSR dissolved.

title: Capital Moved to Astana
description: Kazakhstan moved its capital from Almaty to Astana, signaling national renewal and development.

title: Early Kyrgyz on the Yenisei
description: The Kyrgyz people are first recorded in Chinese sources, originally living near the Yenisei River in Siberia.

title: Kyrgyz Khaganate
description: The Yenisei Kyrgyz defeated the Uyghur Khaganate and established a powerful steppe state.

title: Submission to the Mongols
description: The Kyrgyz submitted to Genghis Khan's expanding empire, becoming part of the Mongol world.

title: Russian Conquest of Kyrgyzstan
description: The Russian Empire fully incorporated Kyrgyz lands following the conquest of the Khanate of Kokand.

title: Independence from the Soviet Union
description: Kyrgyzstan declared independence as the Soviet Union collapsed, with Askar Akayev as first president.

title: Tulip Revolution
description: Mass protests, known as the Tulip Revolution, forced President Akayev from power amid demands for reform.

title: Adoption of Parliamentary System
description: After unrest ousted the president, Kyrgyzstan adopted a new constitution creating a parliamentary democracy.
